title: BURIED BY THE HAND OF GOD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And Moses the servant of the Lord died there in Moab, as the Lord had said. He buried him in Moab, in the valley opposite Beth Peor, but to this day no one knows where his grave is." — Deut 34:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses dies, and Scripture gives him a title of great honour: "the servant of the Lord." That was the summary of his life — not "Moses the great leader" or "Moses the miracle worker," but "the servant of the Lord." To be called God's servant is the highest honour a life can receive. And then comes a remarkable detail: God Himself buried Moses. No human hand laid him to rest; God did. Even in death, Moses was tenderly cared for by the God he had served.

There is something deeply moving in the thought that God buried His servant. It shows us that God's care for His people does not end at death. He tends to us even then, faithful to the very end and beyond. Moses died alone on a mountain, yet he was not alone — God was with him, caring for him even in his burial.

That "no one knows where his grave is" carries its own quiet lesson. There would be no shrine, no place of pilgrimage, no tomb to venerate. The focus was to remain on God, not on Moses. Even the greatest servants point beyond themselves to the Lord they serve.

For those who belong to Christ, death is not the end but a doorway. Jesus has conquered the grave, and He promises that whoever believes in Him will live, even though they die (John 11:25). The God who tenderly buried Moses is the God who holds His people through death and into life. So we need not fear. The faithful God who cares for us in life will care for us in death, and raise us to life everlasting.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Would "servant of the Lord" be a fitting summary of my life?
2. How does it comfort me that God's care doesn't end at death?
3. How does Christ's victory over death change the way I view it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, may my life be summed up as Your faithful servant. Thank You that Your care does not end at death, and that in Christ death is but a doorway to life. Hold me faithfully to the very end and beyond. Amen.
